response: Yes, there is still a need for living-related liver transplantation (LRT) in children. Although the short- and long-term outcomes after LRT and deceased donor liver transplantation (SLT) do not differ significantly, LRT provides a solution for urgent cases where a cadaveric graft cannot be found in time or when the timing of transplantation is critical. This suggests that LRT remains a vital option for pediatric liver transplantation, particularly in situations where a deceased donor organ is not available or when timely transplantation is essential.
